Location
Located on the south-western outskirts of Brigg at Scawby Brook in North Lincolnshire with a national grid reference SE 499850 40610. The installation covers an area of approximately seven hectares and is relatively flat. Land surrounding the site is predominantly farmland. To the south are fields and a local railway track. The New River Anchlome is immediately to the east of the site and beyond this farmland. To the north-east is Island Carr Farm and directly beyond this is mill View Caravan site. To the north of the site are settling ponds beyond this are some residential properties and a sports ground and leisure centre. To the west of the site is the main site access road which passes through open farmland where it meets Scawby Road.

Existing Plant
Four GE Frame 6B Gas Turbines each with electrical generator;
Four redundant Heat Recovery Steam Generators (HRSGs) which have been in preservation since 2013; (these would not form part of the existing CMU)
Two redundant steam turbines currently in preservation each with electrical generator and water-cooled condenser; (these would not form part of the existing CMU)
Cooling towers; and
Connection to the 132000 volt electrical distribution system.
The plant operates using gas from Transcos National Transmission System with the potential to store distillate gas-oil as a standby fuel. 

Metering
Electrical Generation is MVRNd to the BRITGAS trading account. Site Works Power is netted off Total Generation to leave the balance as net export to the National Grid.

Description of CMU Components: TG1 is part of the aggregated CMU EPCMU3, which is made up of 3 Generating Units of which TG1 is of medium size. This Generating Unit is embedded in the E_FAWND BMU and is part of the larger site inclusive BM Trading Unit, EPCo1. All Components of EPCMU3 are located within the physical boundaries of the Esso Petroleum Company Limited Oil Refinery at Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom. TG1 is one of three power and steam generation units on site and is a Steam Turbine plant. It is connected to the Local Distribution Network (LDN) at 132kV level at their Fawley North Sub-Station. All three units share various auxiliary load equipment -  the power for which is supplied from another part of the LDN Fawley North Sub-Station. The auxiliary power is not half hourly metered but does have meters that are manually read monthly. Using the monthly data from the qualification period of the 3 Highest Performance Periods during August 2012 to July 2014 we have determined that on average the TOTAL auxiliary load for all three of the generating units is 7.63 MW which represents 9.85% of the total Power Demand as measured at the metering point MSID 7096. Due to the large amount of common equipment shared by the three generation units we are unable to determine exactly what part of the auxiliary load is directly attributable to TG1 and thus for this CMU we have attributed the auxiliary load evenly about the three units - i.e. 9.855/3 = 3.28% of MSID 7096.   NB. the rest of MSID 7095 is made up of one of our other components of our CMU - Unit 3).
Location and Post Code: SO45 1TX

Description of CMU Components:
Energy from waste facility located in Chineham Hampshire - Postcode RG24 8LL. It is a municipal waste incineration plant. It is based on one boiler supplying steam to one turbine-generator. Exhaust steam is condensed in a Air cooled condenser. The site normally operates at baseload . The auxiliary load is self supplied by the generator prior to export metering.  The power factor used is 0.85 for this CMU.


We found out that using the rules' method to calculate the capacity some of our plants would not be able to meet their obligation. For instance:Tyseley ERF would have to register for 28.74 MW (de-rated to 25.19 MW). And in the past two years during winter period the plant generated that capacity only 45 % of the time. This is due to the plant technology: it is an Energy from waste facility. Waste is a fuel whose characteristics (moisture content-calorific value...) can change during the year and therefore the output of the plants can change a lot. We can therefore have a few high generation periods in the year in the conditions are good and a lower generation the other times.
Therefore we decided to calculate ourselves a capacity we would be confident to register with. We would then compare it to the rules' method calculated value; If the new value is higher than the one calculated with the rules' method then we followed the rules' method. If our method would give a lower capacity; we selected the value calculated with our method.
The method used is: the de rated capacity we are pre-qualifying for to bid is calculated based on the two past years winter historical output (see documents).
The de-rated capacity is calculated as the capacity the plant was able to achieve 80% of the time in the previous two winters. Then the value was multiplied by the inverse of the de-rating factor to obtain the Connection capacity.

In the case of this site : The site would achieve more than 90% of the time the capacity calculated using on of the CM's rules so we followed the rules.

Description of CMU Components:
Statkraft owns and operates the hydro-electric power scheme ?Rheidol? close to Aberystwyth ? Ceredigion - mid-Wales.  The scheme consists of several reservoirs and tunnels and generators. The upper reservoir ?Nant-y-Moch? gathers water from its surrounding hills. From this reservoir the water flows into Dinas Power Station close to Ponterwyd where it drives a 15000 kVA generator (?Generator 1?). The water from the Dinas Power Station as well as additional natural inflow is collected in the Dinas Reservoir. This reservoir supplies water for the largest power station of the scheme namely the Cwm Rheidol Power Station. It consists of two generators with each up to 22500 kVA of capacity (?Generator 2? and ?Generator 3?). At Cwm Rheidol a further reservoir has been created to avoid large variations in the outflow of water. This reservoir collects water that flows through the power station and releases it slowly through a 1250 kVA generator into the Afon Rheidol River. All Generators can be controlled and despatched independently from each other.
Statkraft wishes to apply for two CMU within the Rheidol Hydro Scheme. One will comprise Generator 2 and the other Generator 3. This application relates to Generator 2. 
Metering Configuration:
The Rheidol Hydro Scheme is separated into two Balancing Mechanism Units (?E_RHEI-1? and ?E_RHEI-S?). The Balancing Mechanism Unit ?E_RHEI-1? is the aggregation of the metered output of Generators 1 and 2 and 3. The Balancing Mechanism Unit ?E_RHEI-S? sums up the metered output of minor generation within the scheme. The CMU which Statkraft wishes to pre-qualify consists of solely Generator 2. The output of the Generator is metered individually on a half hourly basis. The MSID for Generator 2 is MSSQ_5025.RHEIGE2MAE.AE. 
Auxiliary Load:
The associated relevant auxiliary load of the CMU Statkraft is applying for (Generator 2) mainly originates from various pumps (oil or drainage) and the supply of the offices with power. In case the Generator is in operation it can be self-supplying through its Unit Auxiliary Transformer. The Unit Auxiliary Transformer extracts the electricity from the main line before (!) it gets metered via the metering apparatus of Generator 2 - already mentioned above. Therefore the metering configurations allow for metering the ?net? output.
But additionally the on-site electricity demand can also be supplied via the Station Auxiliary Transformers 1 and 2. Both Transformers can supply both Generators 2 and 3 as well as the power station itself individually. Therefore the energy entering through the Station Auxiliary Transformers has to be allocated to both Generators. As both Generators comprise the same capacity (22500 kVA) and load patterns it is viable to assume that the supply of energy through the Station Auxiliary Transformers can be split equally with a share of 50:50 to Generator 2 and Generator 3. In 2013 the total auxiliary load metered in both Station Auxiliary Transformers summed up to roughly 500 MWh - resulting in an auxiliary load of 30 kW for each Generator 2 and 3 on average. The meter is being read locally and manually.

Statkraft wishes to apply for two CMU within the Rheidol Hydro Scheme. One will comprise Generator 2 and the other Generator 3. This application relates to Generator 3. 
Metering Configuration:
The Rheidol Hydro Scheme is separated into two Balancing Mechanism Units (?E_RHEI-1? and ?E_RHEI-S?). The Balancing Mechanism Unit ?E_RHEI-1? is the aggregation of the metered output of Generators 1 and 2 and 3. The Balancing Mechanism Unit ?E_RHEI-S? sums up the metered output of minor generation within the scheme. The CMU which Statkraft wishes to pre-qualify consists of solely Generator 3. The output of the Generator is metered individually on a half hourly basis. The MSID for Generator 3 is MSSQ_5025.RHEIGE3MAE.AE. 
Auxiliary Load:
The associated relevant auxiliary load of the CMU Statkraft is applying for (Generator 3) mainly originates from various pumps (oil or drainage) and the supply of the offices with power. In case the Generator is in operation it can be self-supplying through its Unit Auxiliary Transformer. The Unit Auxiliary Transformer extracts the electricity from the main line before (!) it gets metered via the metering apparatus of Generator 3 - already mentioned above. Therefore the metering configurations allow for metering the ?net? output.
But additionally the on-site electricity demand can also be supplied via the Station Auxiliary Transformers 1 and 2. Both Transformers can supply both Generators 2 and 3 as well as the power station itself individually. Therefore the energy entering through the Station Auxiliary Transformers has to be allocated to both Generators. As both Generators comprise the same capacity (22500 kVA) and load patterns it is viable to assume that the supply of energy through the Station Auxiliary Transformers can be split equally with a share of 50:50 to Generator 2 and Generator 3. In 2013 the total auxiliary load metered in both Station Auxiliary Transformers summed up to roughly 500 MWh - resulting in an auxiliary load of 30 kW for each Generator 2 and 3 on average. The meter is being read locally and manually.

Description of CMU Components:
Energy from waste facility located in Staffordshire - Postcode WV10 7DF. This plant was commissionned at the beginning of 2014.  It is a municipal waste incineration plant. It is based on two boilers supplying steam to one turbine-generator. Exhaust steam is condensed in a Air cooled condenser. The site normally operates at baseload. The auxiliary load is self supplied by the generator prior to export metering.  The power factor used is 0.85 for this CMU.

We found out that using the rules' method to calculate the capacity some of our plants would not be able to meet their obligation. For instance:Tyseley ERF would have to register for 28.74 MW (de-rated to 25.19 MW). And in the past two years during winter period the plant generated that capacity only 45 % of the time. This is due to the plant technology: it is an Energy from waste facility. Waste is a fuel whose characteristics (moisture content-calorific value...) can change during the year and therefore the output of the plants can change a lot. We can therefore have a few high generation periods in the year in the conditions are good and a lower generation the other times.
Therefore we decided to calculate ourselves a capacity we would be confident to register with. We would then compare it to the rules' method calculated value; If the new value is higher than the one calculated with the rules' method then we followed the rules' method. If our method would give a lower capacity; we selected the value calculated with our method.
The method used is: the de rated capacity we are pre-qualifying for to bid is calculated based on the two past years winter historical output (see documents).
The de-rated capacity is calculated as the capacity the plant was able to achieve 80% of the time in the previous two winters. Then the value was multiplied by the inverse of the de-rating factor to obtain the Connection capacity.

For this unit the capacity calculted using the CM rules methodology would be achieved more than 90 % of the time we therefore used the CM's rules methodology.
The meters that will be used are the same meter as the one used for the CHPQA accreditation and LECs submissions to OFGEM and the HH settlement meter used for our export contracts.

Description of CMU Components:
Energy from waste facility located in Tyseley Birmingham Postcode B11 2BA. It is a municipal waste incineration plant. It is based on two boilers supplying steam to one turbine generator. Exhaust steam is condensed in a Air cooled condenser. The site normally operates at baseload at 100% capacity. The auxiliary load is self supplied by the generator prior to export metering. The power factor used is 0.85 for this CMU.

We found out that using the rules' method to calculate the capacity some of our plants would not be able to meet their obligation. For instance:Tyseley ERF would have to register for 28.74 MW (de-rated to 25.19 MW). And in the past two years during winter period the plant generated that capacity only 45 % of the time. This is due to the plant technology: it is an Energy from waste facility. Waste is a fuel whose characteristics (moisture content-calorific value...) can change during the year and therefore the output of the plants can change a lot. We can therefore have a few high generation periods in the year in the conditions are good and a lower generation the other times.
Therefore we decided to calculate ourselves a capacity we would be confident to register with. We would then compare it to the rules' method calculated value; If the new value is higher than the one calculated with the rules' method then we followed the rules' method. If our method would give a lower capacity; we selected the value calculated with our method.
The method used is: the de rated capacity we are pre-qualifying for to bid is calculated based on the two past years winter historical output (see documents).
The de-rated capacity is calculated as the capacity the plant was able to achieve 80% of the time in the previous two winters. Then the value was multiplied by the inverse of the de-rating factor to obtain the Connection capacity.

For this plant using the rules we should register for 28.74MW but we would only be able dto provide that 45 % of the time. The value we are able to provide 80 % of the time during winter is a derated capacity of 20.1 MW which means a "re-rated" capacity to register for of 23.39 MW.
The meters that will be used are the same meter as the one used for the CHPQA accreditation and LECs submissions to OFGEM and the HH settlement meter used for our export contracts.

Description of CMU Components: Winnington CHP is an unlicensed (100 MW export limit) non-CMRS Refurbishing Generating CMU which provides heat and power to various adjoining manufacturing sites via pipeline and a large private wire system (Associated Load). It is located in Northwich, Cheshire and consists of three generating units: 1 gas turbine (GT) and 1 steam turbine (ST) (CHP Technology Class) and 1 gas turbine (OCGT technology class). The original configuration of the CHP is 2 x GT 39.97 MW each, both feeding into separate Heat Recovery Boilers, and 1 x ST 58.12 MW (Unit Registered Capacity). These are calculated values from the Distribution Connection and Use of System Agreement values given as: each GT 47.024 MVA, ST 68.38 MVA and using a power factor of 0.85 (also from Connection Agreement). Due to recent (Feb 2014) permanent operational changes resulting in a significant reduction in steam demand from the CHP Plant, the 58.12 MW steam turbine can no longer be operated. Winnington CHP Ltd is therefore applying as a refurbishing CMU as the old ST is being replaced by a new, correctly sized ST (14.63 MW) to be commissioned in September 2015. The new steam turbine has been ordered and approximately £1.3m of the £5.5m project cost has been incurred already. As a consequence, the refurbishment is a capacity reduction. The CHP Plant parasitic load is 3 MW and the CHP supplies on average 13.74 MW to four other users at two different locations in Northwich (Winnington and Lostock) by private wire (Tata Chemicals Europe Ltd (TCE) Winnington: 3.33 MW, TCE Lostock: 5.53 MW, Ineos Winnington: 0.47 MW, Ineos Lostock: 4.41 MW). The calculation methods used for the Available Capacity of each generating unit are based on Rule 3.5.2(c)(iii)(bb) for the new ST and Rule 3.5.2(c)(i) for both GT?s. The parasitic and associated loads were prorated and assigned to each generating unit without weighting to obtain the Available Capacity of each unit. The Anticipated De-rated Capacity of the CMU is 71.25 MW. Winnington CHP exports to the Distribution system via a single MPAN, at 132KV. The connection agreement permits an export in excess of the Anticipated De-rated capacity of the refurbished CMU.

It is located in Northwich, Cheshire and consists of three generating units: 1 gas turbine (GT) and 1 steam turbine (ST) (CHP Technology Class) and 1 gas turbine (OCGT technology class). The original configuration of the CHP is 2 x GT 39.97 MW each, both feeding into separate Heat Recovery Boilers, and 1 x ST 58.12 MW (Unit Registered Capacity). These are calculated values from the Distribution Connection and Use of System Agreement values given as: each GT 47.024 MVA, ST 68.38 MVA and using a power factor of 0.85 (also from Connection Agreement). Due to recent (Feb 2014) permanent operational changes resulting in a significant reduction in steam demand from the CHP Plant, the 58.12 MW steam turbine can no longer be operated. Winnington CHP Ltd is therefore applying as a refurbishing CMU as the old ST is being replaced by a new, correctly sized ST (14.63 MW) to be commissioned in September 2015. The new steam turbine has been ordered and approximately £1.3m of the £5.5m project cost has been incurred already. As a consequence, the refurbishment is a capacity reduction. The CHP Plant parasitic load is 3 MW and the CHP supplies on average 13.74 MW to four other users at two different locations in Northwich (Winnington and Lostock) by private wire (Tata Chemicals Europe Ltd (TCE) Winnington: 3.33 MW, TCE Lostock: 5.53 MW, Ineos Winnington: 0.47 MW, Ineos Lostock: 4.41 MW). The calculation methods used for the Available Capacity of each generating unit are based on Rule 3.5.2(c)(iii)(bb) for the new ST and Rule 3.5.2(c)(i) for both GT?s. The parasitic and associated loads were prorated and assigned to each generating unit without weighting to obtain the Available Capacity of each unit. The Anticipated De-rated Capacity of the CMU is 71.25 MW. Winnington CHP exports to the Distribution system via a single MPAN, at 132KV. The connection agreement permits an export in excess of the Anticipated De-rated capacity of the refurbished CMU.

Description of CMU Components:
TG1B is part of the aggregated CMU EMD-18, which is made up of 2 Generating Units of which TG1B is the larger. 

This Generating Unit is embedded in the 'E_FAWND BMU' and is part of the larger site inclusive BM Trading Unit, 'EPCO1'. All Components of 'EMD-18' are located within the physical boundaries of the Esso Petroleum Company,Limited Oil Refinery at Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom. 

TG1B is one of three power and steam generation units on the site and is a Steam Turbine plant. It is connected to the Local Distribution Network (LDN) at 132kV level at the Fawley North Sub-Station (part of MSID 7095). Both Unit 3 and TG1B units share various auxiliary load equipment- the power for which is supplied from another part of the LDN Fawley North Sub-Station. 

There is a project currently in construction phase to install separate metering for the auxiliary power for both TG1B and Unit 3. This will provide half hourly meters for the auxiliary load for the two units, these will be installed in time to pass a Metering Test for the delivery of this Capacity Market (they are planned for completion on 28th September 2018). This was previously agreed with the settlements body as part of an appeal process for the T-4 2018 capacity market auction. In this appeal the capacity market settlements body accepted ExxonMobil's appeal for the auxiliary meters to be installed in time for the capacity market delivery period 2018/19 i.e. 1st October 2018. 

For now, using the same method as for the T4 -2018 Capacity Market, (with the successful appeal) we have determined the auxiliary load for TG1B to be 2.024 MW (based on the total auxiliary consumption over the three Highest TG1B+Unit 3 Generation points) which represents on average 7.954% of the total Power Demand as measured at the metering points at MSID 7096. 

Due to the large amount of common equipment shared by the three generation units we are unable to determine exactly what part of the auxiliary load is directly attributable to TG1B and thus for this CMU we have attributed the auxiliary load evenly about the three units - i.e. 7.954/3 = 2.6513% of MSID 7096, thus 2.024 MW.   (NB. the rest of MSID 7095 is made up of one of our other components of our CMU- i.e. Unit 3). 

To clarify the 3 units within the refinery boundary, they are Unit 5 (EMG-18) and TG1B and Unit 3 (which make up EMD-18). Unit 5 now has half hourly meters installed on the auxiliary load so the estimate on auxiliary load for now is only for Unit 3 and TG1B. This will move to half hourly metering for Unit 3 and TG1B once the auxiliary load meters are installed by 28th September 2018.

Gross 3 HH av. peak generation from TG1B on separate days = 56.634 MW
At these three HH times, aux load on TG1B = 2.024 MW
Net generation from TG1B = 54.610 MW

Description of CMU Components:
TG1B is part of the aggregated CMU EMD-19, which is made up of 2 Generating Units of which TG1B is the larger. 

This Generating Unit is embedded in the 'E_FAWND' BMU and is part of the larger site inclusive BM Trading Unit, 'EPCO1'. All Components of 'EMD-19' are located within the physical boundaries of the Esso Petroleum Company,Limited Oil Refinery at Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom. 

TG1B is one of three power generation units on the site and is a Steam Turbine plant. It is connected to the Local Distribution Network (LDN) at 132kV level at the Fawley North Sub-Station (part of MSID 7095). Both Unit 3 and TG1B units share various auxiliary load equipment- the power for which is supplied from another part of the LDN Fawley North Sub-Station. 

Installation of separate metering for the auxiliary power for both TG1B and Unit 3 has been completed providing half hourly meters for the auxiliary load for the two units. 

Due to the large amount of common equipment shared by the two generation units (TG1B and Unit 3) we are unable to determine exactly what part of the auxiliary load is directly attributable to TG1B and thus for this CMU we have attributed the auxiliary load between the two. The auxiliary meters for Unit 3 and TG1B combined are: TR1MWI_MAIN, TR2MWI_MAIN and 26AMWI_MAIN. This entire metering configuration has been successfully assessed and tested. 

To clarify the 3 units within the refinery boundary, they are Unit 5 (EMG-19) and TG1B and Unit 3 (which make up EMD-19).  

Gross 3 HH av. peak generation from TG1B on separate days = 49.863 MW
At these three HH times, aux load on TG1B = -1.468 MW
Net generation from TG1B = 48.394 MW

Description of CMU Components:
The Consortium (TEPCO and NGK) will provide the service from a Sodium Sulfur (NAS®) battery system with Power Conversion System (PCS) (rated capacity: 10MW (short-time rating: 11MW) /60MWh) and control system which will be fully commissioned by TEPCO and NGK.  The system can be configured to provide two alternative service arrangements.  One is to provide Balancing Services of Enhanced or Firm Frequency Response as well as an energy delivery service for Capacity Market, and the other is to provide triad avoidance service to its customer (Honda) during the time except service period of Frequency Response Services in Winter.

The NAS battery is commercially produced by NGK and more than 530 MW and 3700 MWh have been installed globally.  The NAS battery has been used by more than 190 customers and has been used in similar applications in many installations. 

The assets comprise 10MW (short-time rating: 11 MW)/60MWh of battery modules, which will be packaged in bespoke shipping containers with built-in battery management system, connected to a system controller and a power conversion system.  The assets are connected to the 33 kV network connection through an existing connection on the premises of Honda of the UK Manufacturing Limited. of approximately 4500 m2 required for minimum ground works.   

In accordance with the terms of the Capacity Market Rules, if the Applicant?s Bid is successful then the Applicant will incorporate a special purpose vehicle company (to be incorporated in England and Wales) (?JVCO?), and the Applicant intends, subject to the approval of EMR Delivery Body, for the Capacity Market Contract to be entered into between EMR Delivering Body and JVCO.
Location and Post Code: The Site will be on the premises of Honda of the UK Manufacturing Limited (?Honda UK") located at Highworth Road, South Marston, Swindon, Wiltshire, SN3 4TZ.

All Components of EM3-21 are located within the physical boundaries of the Esso Petroleum Company Limited Oil Refinery at Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom. TG1B is one of three power and steam generation units on site and is a Steam Turbine plant. It is connected to the Local Distribution Network (LDN) at 132kV level at their Fawley North Sub-Station (part of MSID 7095). All three units share various auxiliary load equipment -  the power for which is supplied from another part of the LDN Fawley North Sub-Station. The auxiliary power will have half hourly meters, these will be installed in time to pass a Metering Test for this Capacity Market. For now, using the same method as for the T4 -2018 Capacity Market, we have determined this to be ~ 7.72s MW (maximum consumption over the three Highest Generation points) which represents 9.79% of the total Power Demand as measured at the metering points at MSID 7096. Due to the large amount of common equipment shared by the three generation units we are unable to determine exactly what part of the auxiliary load is directly attributable to TG1B and thus for this CMU we have attributed the auxiliary load evenly about the three units - i.e. 9.79/3 = 3.26% of MSID 7096, thus 2.574 MW.   (NB. the rest of MSID 7095 is made up of one of our other components of our CMU - Unit 3).

ElecLink will have a transmission capacity of 1000MW corresponding to its grid connection agreements and link the 400kV AC grids of France and Great Britain. ElecLink will employ high voltage direct current converter stations using voltage source converter technology at each side of the Channel Tunnel. 400kV AC underground cables will connect the converter stations to the TSO's high voltage substations: Sellindge (NGET, UK) and Les Mandarins (RTE, France).

Description of CMU Components:
TG1B is part of the aggregated CMU EMD-19, which is made up of 2 Generating Units of which TG1B is the larger. 

This Generating Unit is embedded in the 'E_FAWND' BMU and is part of the larger site inclusive BM Trading Unit, 'EPCO1'. All Components of 'EMD-19' are located within the physical boundaries of the Esso Petroleum Company,Limited Oil Refinery at Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom. 

TG1B is one of three power generation units on the site and is a Steam Turbine plant. It is connected to the Local Distribution Network (LDN) at 132kV level at the Fawley North Sub-Station (part of MSID 7095). Both Unit 3 and TG1B units share various auxiliary load equipment- the power for which is supplied from another part of the LDN Fawley North Sub-Station. 

Installation of separate metering for the auxiliary power for both TG1B and Unit 3 has been completed providing half hourly meters for the auxiliary load for the two units. 

Due to the large amount of common equipment shared by the two generation units (TG1B and Unit 3) we are unable to determine exactly what part of the auxiliary load is directly attributable to TG1B and thus for this CMU we have attributed the auxiliary load between the two. The auxiliary meters for Unit 3 and TG1B combined are: TR1MWI_MAIN, TR2MWI_MAIN and 26AMWI_MAIN. This entire metering configuration has been successfully assessed and tested. 

To clarify the 3 units within the refinery boundary, they are Unit 5 (EMG-19) and TG1B and Unit 3 (which make up EMD-19).  

Gross 3 HH av. peak generation from TG1B on separate days = 49.863 MW
At these three HH times, aux load on TG1B = -1.468 MW
Net generation from TG1B = 48.394 MW
Location and Post Code: Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom

ElecLink will have a transmission capacity of 1000MW corresponding to its grid connection agreements and link the 400kV AC grids of France and Great Britain. ElecLink will employ high voltage direct current converter stations using voltage source converter technology at each side of the Channel Tunnel. 400kV AC underground cables will connect the converter stations to the TSO's high voltage substations: Sellindge (NGET, UK) and Les Mandarins (RTE, France). 

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Folkestone will be connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the National Grid substation at Sellindge. The route length is approximately 14km.

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Coquelles will be connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the RTE substation at Les Madarins. The route length is approximately 3.5km.

An approximately 52km long HVDC cable circuit will connect the two converter stations via the Channel Tunnel between Folkestone and Coquelles. This will involve two single-core HVDC cables operating at +-320kV DC.

Description of CMU Components:
TG1B is part of the aggregated CMU EMD-18, which is made up of 2 Generating Units of which TG1B is the larger. 

This Generating Unit is embedded in the 'E_FAWND BMU' and is part of the larger site inclusive BM Trading Unit, 'EPCO1'. All Components of 'EMD-18' are located within the physical boundaries of the Esso Petroleum Company,Limited Oil Refinery at Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom. 

TG1B is one of three power and steam generation units on the site and is a Steam Turbine plant. It is connected to the Local Distribution Network (LDN) at 132kV level at the Fawley North Sub-Station (part of MSID 7095). Both Unit 3 and TG1B units share various auxiliary load equipment- the power for which is supplied from another part of the LDN Fawley North Sub-Station. 

There is a project currently in construction phase to install separate metering for the auxiliary power for both TG1B and Unit 3. This will provide half hourly meters for the auxiliary load for the two units, these will be installed in time to pass a Metering Test for the delivery of this Capacity Market (they are planned for completion on 28th September 2018). This was previously agreed with the settlements body as part of an appeal process for the T-4 2018 capacity market auction. In this appeal the capacity market settlements body accepted ExxonMobil's appeal for the auxiliary meters to be installed in time for the capacity market delivery period 2018/19 i.e. 1st October 2018. 

For now, using the same method as for the T4 -2018 Capacity Market, (with the successful appeal) we have determined the auxiliary load for TG1B to be 2.024 MW (based on the total auxiliary consumption over the three Highest TG1B+Unit 3 Generation points) which represents on average 7.954% of the total Power Demand as measured at the metering points at MSID 7096. 

Due to the large amount of common equipment shared by the three generation units we are unable to determine exactly what part of the auxiliary load is directly attributable to TG1B and thus for this CMU we have attributed the auxiliary load evenly about the three units - i.e. 7.954/3 = 2.6513% of MSID 7096, thus 2.024 MW.   (NB. the rest of MSID 7095 is made up of one of our other components of our CMU- i.e. Unit 3). 

To clarify the 3 units within the refinery boundary, they are Unit 5 (EMG-18) and TG1B and Unit 3 (which make up EMD-18). Unit 5 now has half hourly meters installed on the auxiliary load so the estimate on auxiliary load for now is only for Unit 3 and TG1B. This will move to half hourly metering for Unit 3 and TG1B once the auxiliary load meters are installed by 28th September 2018.

Gross 3 HH av. peak generation from TG1B on separate days = 56.634 MW
At these three HH times, aux load on TG1B = 2.024 MW
Net generation from TG1B = 54.610 MW
Location and Post Code: Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom

ElecLink will have a transmission capacity of 1000MW corresponding to its grid connection agreements and link the 400kV AC grids of France and Great Britain. ElecLink will employ high voltage direct current converter stations using voltage source converter technology at each side of the Channel Tunnel. 400kV AC underground cables will connect the converter stations to the TSO's high voltage substations: Sellindge (NGET, UK) and Les Mandarins (RTE, France). 

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Folkestone will be connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the National Grid substation at Sellindge. The route length is approximately 14km.

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Coquelles will be connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the RTE substation at Les Madarins. The route length is approximately 3.5km.

An approximately 52km long HVDC cable circuit will connect the two converter stations via the Channel Tunnel between Folkestone and Coquelles. This will involve two single-core HVDC cables operating at +-320kV DC.

Description of CMU Components:
TG1B is part of the aggregated CMU EMD-19, which is made up of 2 Generating Units of which TG1B is the larger. 

This Generating Unit is embedded in the 'E_FAWND' BMU and is part of the larger site inclusive BM Trading Unit, 'EPCO1'. All Components of 'EMD-19' are located within the physical boundaries of the Esso Petroleum Company,Limited Oil Refinery at Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom. 

TG1B is one of three power generation units on the site and is a Steam Turbine plant. It is connected to the Local Distribution Network (LDN) at 132kV level at the Fawley North Sub-Station (part of MSID 7095). Both Unit 3 and TG1B units share various auxiliary load equipment- the power for which is supplied from another part of the LDN Fawley North Sub-Station. 

Installation of separate metering for the auxiliary power for both TG1B and Unit 3 has been completed providing half hourly meters for the auxiliary load for the two units. 

Due to the large amount of common equipment shared by the two generation units (TG1B and Unit 3) we are unable to determine exactly what part of the auxiliary load is directly attributable to TG1B and thus for this CMU we have attributed the auxiliary load between the two. The auxiliary meters for Unit 3 and TG1B combined are: TR1MWI_MAIN, TR2MWI_MAIN and 26AMWI_MAIN. This entire metering configuration has been successfully assessed and tested. 

To clarify the 3 units within the refinery boundary, they are Unit 5 (EMG-19) and TG1B and Unit 3 (which make up EMD-19).  

Gross 3 HH av. peak generation from TG1B on separate days = 49.863 MW
At these three HH times, aux load on TG1B = -1.468 MW
Net generation from TG1B = 48.394 MW
Location and Post Code: Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom

ElecLink will have a transmission capacity of 1000MW corresponding to its grid connection agreements and link the 400kV AC grids of France and Great Britain. ElecLink will employ high voltage direct current converter stations using voltage source converter technology at each side of the Channel Tunnel. 400kV AC underground cables will connect the converter stations to the TSO's high voltage substations: Sellindge (NGET, UK) and Les Mandarins (RTE, France). 

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Folkestone will be connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the National Grid substation at Sellindge. The route length is approximately 14km.

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Coquelles will be connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the RTE substation at Les Madarins. The route length is approximately 3.5km.

An approximately 52km long HVDC cable circuit will connect the two converter stations via the Channel Tunnel between Folkestone and Coquelles. This will involve two single-core HVDC cables operating at +-320kV DC.

Description of CMU Components:
TG1B is part of the aggregated CMU EMD-19, which is made up of 2 Generating Units of which TG1B is the larger. 

This Generating Unit is embedded in the 'E_FAWND' BMU and is part of the larger site inclusive BM Trading Unit, 'EPCO1'. All Components of 'EMD-19' are located within the physical boundaries of the Esso Petroleum Company,Limited Oil Refinery at Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom. 

TG1B is one of three power generation units on the site and is a Steam Turbine plant. It is connected to the Local Distribution Network (LDN) at 132kV level at the Fawley North Sub-Station (part of MSID 7095). Both Unit 3 and TG1B units share various auxiliary load equipment- the power for which is supplied from another part of the LDN Fawley North Sub-Station. 

Installation of separate metering for the auxiliary power for both TG1B and Unit 3 has been completed providing half hourly meters for the auxiliary load for the two units. 

Due to the large amount of common equipment shared by the two generation units (TG1B and Unit 3) we are unable to determine exactly what part of the auxiliary load is directly attributable to TG1B and thus for this CMU we have attributed the auxiliary load between the two. The auxiliary meters for Unit 3 and TG1B combined are: TR1MWI_MAIN, TR2MWI_MAIN and 26AMWI_MAIN. This entire metering configuration has been successfully assessed and tested. 

To clarify the 3 units within the refinery boundary, they are Unit 5 (EMG-19) and TG1B and Unit 3 (which make up EMD-19).  

Gross 3 HH av. peak generation from TG1B on separate days = 49.863 MW
At these three HH times, aux load on TG1B = -1.468 MW
Net generation from TG1B = 48.394 MW

Description of CMU Components:
TG1B is part of the aggregated CMU EMD-20, which is made up of 2 Generating Units of which TG1B is the larger. 

This Generating Unit is embedded in the 'E_FAWND' BMU and is part of the larger site inclusive BM Trading Unit, 'EPCO1'. All Components of 'EMD-20' are located within the physical boundaries of the Esso Petroleum Company,Limited Oil Refinery at Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom. 

TG1B is one of three power generation units on the site and is a Steam Turbine plant. It is connected to the Local Distribution Network (LDN) at 132kV level at the Fawley North Sub-Station (part of MSID 7095). Both Unit 3 and TG1B units share various auxiliary load equipment- the power for which is supplied from another part of the LDN Fawley North Sub-Station. 

Installation of separate metering for the auxiliary power for both TG1B and Unit 3 has been completed providing half hourly meters for the auxiliary load for the two units. 

Due to the large amount of common equipment shared by the two generation units (TG1B and Unit 3) we are unable to determine exactly what part of the auxiliary load is directly attributable to TG1B and thus for this CMU we have attributed the auxiliary load between the two. The auxiliary meters for Unit 3 and TG1B combined are: TR1MWI_MAIN, TR2MWI_MAIN and 26AMWI_MAIN. This entire metering configuration has been successfully assessed and tested. 

To clarify the 3 units within the refinery boundary, they are Unit 5 (EMG-20) and TG1B and Unit 3 (which make up EMD-20).  

Gross 3 HH av. peak generation from TG1B on separate days = 49.863 MW
At these three HH times, aux load on TG1B = -1.468 MW
Net generation from TG1B = 48.394 MW

The 48.394MW described above is the historical proven capacity. However, based on the planned future availability of this unit, we wish to submit a conservative 18MW connection capacity.

To clarify the numbers provided in the application page are in half hourly periods, as the units specified were MWh and therefore reporting half hourly period was required.
Location and Post Code: Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom

Description of CMU Components:
ElecLink will have a transmission capacity of 1000MW corresponding to its grid connection agreements and link the 400kV AC grids of France and Great Britain. ElecLink will employ high voltage direct current converter stations using voltage source converter technology at each side of the Channel Tunnel. 400kV AC underground cables will connect the converter stations to the TSO's high voltage substations: Sellindge (NGET, UK) and Les Mandarins (RTE, France). 

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Folkestone will be connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the National Grid substation at Sellindge. The route length is approximately 14km.

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Coquelles will be connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the RTE substation at Les Madarins. The route length is approximately 3.5km.

An approximately 52km long HVDC cable circuit will connect the two converter stations via the Channel Tunnel between Folkestone and Coquelles. This will involve two single-core HVDC cables operating at +-320kV DC.

Description of CMU Components:
HVDC interconnector between GB and Danish transmission systems. 

Viking Link will involve the construction of two converter stations, sited in GB and Denmark. At the converter stations, alternating current electricity from the sending end is converted to direct current electricity and transmitted through the cables. The direct current electricity will be converted into alternating current at the receiving end, before it is transmitted to consumers via the onshore electricity networks in GB and Denmark.

In GB, the grid connection point for Viking Link is at Bicker Fen substation. The converter station at North Ing Drove is 2km from the substation which is connected via AC underground cables. From the converter station, the British onshore section covers 68km of HVDC underground cable to the landfall point of Boygrift which marks the beginning of the offshore route. The marine section of the link has a total of 621km from Boygrift to the Danish landing point of Blaabjerg through British, Dutch, German and Danish waters. From the Danish landfall point in Blaabjerg the Danish onshore section of Viking Link covers 76km of HVDC underground cable to the converter station which is adjacent to the Revsing substation.

Description of CMU Components:
TG1B is part of the aggregated CMU EMD241, which is made up of 2 Generating Units of which TG1B is the larger. 

This Generating Unit is embedded in the 'E_FAWND' BMU and is part of the larger site inclusive BM Trading Unit, 'EPCO1'. All Components of 'EMD241' are located within the physical boundaries of the Esso Petroleum Company,Limited Oil Refinery at Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom. 

TG1B is one of three power generation units on the site and is a Steam Turbine plant. It is connected to the Local Distribution Network (LDN) at 132kV level at the Fawley North Sub-Station (part of MSID 7095). Both Unit 3 and TG1B units share various auxiliary load equipment, the power for which is supplied from another part of the LDN Fawley North Sub-Station.

Installation of separate metering for the auxiliary power for both TG1B and Unit 3 has been completed providing half hourly meters for the auxiliary load for the two units. Due to the large amount of common equipment shared by the two generation units (TG1B and Unit 3) we are unable to determine exactly what part of the auxiliary load is directly attributable to TG1B and thus for this CMU we have attributed the auxiliary load between the two. The auxiliary meters for Unit 3 and TG1B combined are: TR1MWI_MAIN, TR2MWI_MAIN and 26AMWI_MAIN. This entire metering configuration has been successfully assessed and tested.
Location and Post Code: Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom

Description of CMU Components:
ElecLink will have a transmission capacity of 1000MW corresponding to its grid connection agreements and link the 400kV AC grids of France and Great Britain. ElecLink will employ high voltage direct current converter stations using voltage source converter technology at each side of the Channel Tunnel. 400kV AC underground cables will connect the converter stations to the TSO's high voltage substations: Sellindge (NGET, UK) and Les Mandarins (RTE, France). 

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Folkestone will be connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the National Grid substation at Sellindge. The route length is approximately 14km.

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Coquelles will be connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the RTE substation at Les Madarins. The route length is approximately 3.5km.

An approximately 52km long HVDC cable circuit will connect the two converter stations via the Channel Tunnel between Folkestone and Coquelles. This will involve two single-core HVDC cables operating at +-320kV DC.

Description of CMU Components:
HVDC interconnector between GB and Danish transmission systems. 

Viking Link will involve the construction of two converter stations, sited in GB and Denmark. At the converter stations, alternating current electricity from the sending end is converted to direct current electricity and transmitted through the cables. The direct current electricity will be converted into alternating current at the receiving end, before it is transmitted to consumers via the onshore electricity networks in GB and Denmark.

In GB, the grid connection point for Viking Link is at Bicker Fen substation. The converter station at North Ing Drove is 2km from the substation which is connected via AC underground cables. From the converter station, the British onshore section covers 68km of HVDC underground cable to the landfall point of Boygrift which marks the beginning of the offshore route. The marine section of the link has a total of 621km from Boygrift to the Danish landing point of Blaabjerg through British, Dutch, German and Danish waters. From the Danish landfall point in Blaabjerg the Danish onshore section of Viking Link covers 76km of HVDC underground cable to the converter station which is adjacent to the Revsing substation.

Description of CMU Components:
TG1B is part of the aggregated CMU EMD-19, which is made up of 2 Generating Units of which TG1B is the larger. 

This Generating Unit is embedded in the 'E_FAWND' BMU and is part of the larger site inclusive BM Trading Unit, 'EPCO1'. All Components of 'EMD-19' are located within the physical boundaries of the Esso Petroleum Company,Limited Oil Refinery at Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom. 

TG1B is one of three power generation units on the site and is a Steam Turbine plant. It is connected to the Local Distribution Network (LDN) at 132kV level at the Fawley North Sub-Station (part of MSID 7095). Both Unit 3 and TG1B units share various auxiliary load equipment- the power for which is supplied from another part of the LDN Fawley North Sub-Station. 

Installation of separate metering for the auxiliary power for both TG1B and Unit 3 has been completed providing half hourly meters for the auxiliary load for the two units. 

Due to the large amount of common equipment shared by the two generation units (TG1B and Unit 3) we are unable to determine exactly what part of the auxiliary load is directly attributable to TG1B and thus for this CMU we have attributed the auxiliary load between the two. The auxiliary meters for Unit 3 and TG1B combined are: TR1MWI_MAIN, TR2MWI_MAIN and 26AMWI_MAIN. This entire metering configuration has been successfully assessed and tested. 

To clarify the 3 units within the refinery boundary, they are Unit 5 (EMG-19) and TG1B and Unit 3 (which make up EMD-19).  

Gross 3 HH av. peak generation from TG1B on separate days = 49.863 MW
At these three HH times, aux load on TG1B = -1.468 MW
Net generation from TG1B = 48.394 MW
Location and Post Code: Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom

Description of CMU Components:
ElecLink has a transmission capacity of 1000MW corresponding to its grid connection agreements and link the 400kV AC grids of France and Great Britain. ElecLink employs voltage direct current converter stations using voltage source converter technology at each side of the Channel Tunnel. 400kV AC underground cables connect the converter stations to the TSO's high voltage substations: Sellindge (NGET, UK) and Les Mandarins (RTE, France). 

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Folkestone will be connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the National Grid substation at Sellindge. The route length is approximately 14km.

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Coquelles will be connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the RTE substation at Les Madarins. The route length is approximately 3.5km.

An approximately 52km long HVDC cable circuit will connect the two converter stations via the Channel Tunnel between Folkestone and Coquelles. This will involve two single-core HVDC cables operating at +-320kV DC.

Description of CMU Components:
HVDC interconnector between GB and Danish transmission systems. 

Viking Link will involve the construction of two converter stations, sited in GB and Denmark. At the converter stations, alternating current electricity from the sending end is converted to direct current electricity and transmitted through the cables. The direct current electricity will be converted into alternating current at the receiving end, before it is transmitted to consumers via the onshore electricity networks in GB and Denmark.

In GB, the grid connection point for Viking Link is at Bicker Fen substation. The converter station at North Ing Drove is 2km from the substation which is connected via AC underground cables. From the converter station, the British onshore section covers 68km of HVDC underground cable to the landfall point of Boygrift which marks the beginning of the offshore route. The marine section of the link has a total of 621km from Boygrift to the Danish landing point of Blaabjerg through British, Dutch, German and Danish waters. From the Danish landfall point in Blaabjerg the Danish onshore section of Viking Link covers 76km of HVDC underground cable to the converter station which is adjacent to the Revsing substation.
Location and Post Code: Viking Link, Bicker Fen Converter Station, North Ing Drove, Donnington, Spalding, Lincolnshire, PE11 4XY

Description of CMU Components:
TG1B is part of the aggregated CMU EMD-19, which is made up of 2 Generating Units of which TG1B is the larger. 

This Generating Unit is embedded in the 'E_FAWND' BMU and is part of the larger site inclusive BM Trading Unit, 'EPCO1'. All Components of 'EMD-19' are located within the physical boundaries of the Esso Petroleum Company,Limited Oil Refinery at Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom. 

TG1B is one of three power generation units on the site and is a Steam Turbine plant. It is connected to the Local Distribution Network (LDN) at 132kV level at the Fawley North Sub-Station (part of MSID 7095). Both Unit 3 and TG1B units share various auxiliary load equipment- the power for which is supplied from another part of the LDN Fawley North Sub-Station. 

Installation of separate metering for the auxiliary power for both TG1B and Unit 3 has been completed providing half hourly meters for the auxiliary load for the two units. 

Due to the large amount of common equipment shared by the two generation units (TG1B and Unit 3) we are unable to determine exactly what part of the auxiliary load is directly attributable to TG1B and thus for this CMU we have attributed the auxiliary load between the two. The auxiliary meters for Unit 3 and TG1B combined are: TR1MWI_MAIN, TR2MWI_MAIN and 26AMWI_MAIN. This entire metering configuration has been successfully assessed and tested. 

To clarify the 3 units within the refinery boundary, they are Unit 5 (EMG-19) and TG1B and Unit 3 (which make up EMD-19).  

Gross 3 HH av. peak generation from TG1B on separate days = 49.863 MW
At these three HH times, aux load on TG1B = -1.468 MW
Net generation from TG1B = 48.394 MW
Location and Post Code: Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom

ElecLink has a transmission capacity of 1000MW corresponding to its grid connection agreements and link the 400kV AC grids of France and Great Britain. ElecLink employs voltage direct current converter stations using voltage source converter technology at each side of the Channel Tunnel. 400kV AC underground cables connect the converter stations to the TSO's high voltage substations: Sellindge (NGET, UK) and Les Mandarins (RTE, France). 

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Folkestone is connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the National Grid substation at Sellindge. The route length is approximately 14km.

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Coquelles is connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the RTE substation at Les Madarins. The route length is approximately 3.5km.

An approximately 52km long HVDC cable circuit connects the two converter stations via the Channel Tunnel between Folkestone and Coquelles. This involves two single-core HVDC cables operating at +-320kV DC.

Description of CMU Components:
HVDC interconnector between GB and Danish transmission systems. 

Viking Link will involve the construction of two converter stations, sited in GB and Denmark. At the converter stations, alternating current electricity from the sending end is converted to direct current electricity and transmitted through the cables. The direct current electricity will be converted into alternating current at the receiving end, before it is transmitted to consumers via the onshore electricity networks in GB and Denmark.

In GB, the grid connection point for Viking Link is at Bicker Fen substation. The converter station at North Ing Drove is 2km from the substation which is connected via AC underground cables. From the converter station, the British onshore section covers 68km of HVDC underground cable to the landfall point of Boygrift which marks the beginning of the offshore route. The marine section of the link has a total of 621km from Boygrift to the Danish landing point of Blaabjerg through British, Dutch, German and Danish waters. From the Danish landfall point in Blaabjerg the Danish onshore section of Viking Link covers 76km of HVDC underground cable to the converter station which is adjacent to the Revsing substation.
Location and Post Code: Viking Link Ltd, Bicker Fen Converter Station, Northorpe Road, Donington SPALDING PE11 4XY

All Components of 'EMD244' are located within the physical boundaries of the Esso Petroleum Company,Limited Oil Refinery at Esso Refinery - Fawley - Southampton - Hampshire - SO45 1TX - United Kingdom. 

TG1B is one of three power generation units on the site and is a Steam Turbine plant. It is connected to the Local Distribution Network (LDN) at 132kV level at the Fawley North Sub-Station (part of MSID 7095). Both Unit 3 and TG1B units share various auxiliary load equipment, the power for which is supplied from another part of the LDN Fawley North Sub-Station. 

Installation of separate metering for the auxiliary power for both TG1B and Unit 3 has been completed providing half hourly meters for the auxiliary load for the two units. Due to the large amount of common equipment shared by the two generation units (TG1B and Unit 3) we are unable to determine exactly what part of the auxiliary load is directly attributable to TG1B and thus for this CMU we have attributed the auxiliary load between the two. The auxiliary meters for Unit 3 and TG1B combined are: TR1MWI_MAIN, TR2MWI_MAIN and 26AMWI_MAIN. This entire metering configuration has been successfully assessed and tested.

ElecLink has a transmission capacity of 1000MW corresponding to its grid connection agreements and link the 400kV AC grids of France and Great Britain. ElecLink employs voltage direct current converter stations using voltage source converter technology at each side of the Channel Tunnel. 400kV AC underground cables connect the converter stations to the TSO's high voltage substations: Sellindge (NGET, UK) and Les Mandarins (RTE, France). 

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Folkestone is connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the National Grid substation at Sellindge. The route length is approximately 14km.

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Coquelles is connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the RTE substation at Les Madarins. The route length is approximately 3.5km.

An approximately 52km long HVDC cable circuit connects the two converter stations via the Channel Tunnel between Folkestone and Coquelles. This involves two single-core HVDC cables operating at +-320kV DC.

Description of CMU Components:
Viking Link is a HVDC interconnector between GB and Danish transmission systems. 
Viking Link involved the construction of two converter stations, sited in GB and Denmark. At the converter stations, alternating current electricity from the sending end is converted to direct current electricity and transmitted through the cables. The direct current electricity is converted into alternating current at the receiving end, before it is transmitted to consumers via the onshore electricity networks in GB and Denmark.
In GB, the grid connection point for Viking Link is at Bicker Fen substation. The converter station at North Ing Drove is 2km from the substation which is connected via AC underground cables. From the converter station, the British onshore section covers 68km of HVDC underground cable to the landfall point of Boygrift which marks the beginning of the offshore route. The marine section of the link has a total of 621km from Boygrift to the Danish landing point of Blaabjerg through British, Dutch, German and Danish waters. From the Danish landfall point in Blaabjerg the Danish onshore section of Viking Link covers 76km of HVDC underground cable to the converter station which is adjacent to the Revsing substation.
Location and Post Code: Viking Link Ltd, Bicker Fen Converter Station, Northorpe Road, Donington SPALDING PE11 4XY

Description of CMU Components:
Eleclink has a transmission capacity of 1000MW corresponding to its grid connection agreements and links the 400kV AC grids of France and Great Britain. Eleclink employs voltage direct current converter stations using voltage source converter technology at each side of the Channel Tunnel. 400kV AC underground cables connect the converter stations to the TSO's high voltage substations: Sellindge (NGET, UK) and Les Mandarins (RTE, France). 

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Folkestone is connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the National Grid substation at Sellindge. The route length is approximately 14km.

The converter station on the Eurotunnel site at Coquelles is connected by one 400kV AC cable circuit to the RTE substation at Les Madarins. The route length is approximately 3.5km.

An approximately 52km long HVDC cable circuit connects the two converter stations via the Channel Tunnel between Folkestone and Coquelles. This involves two single-core HVDC cables operating at +-320kV DC.

Please note that in the section below we provided an address for the CMU which relates to the UK substation site at Sellindge, given this is the location of the Eleclink interconnector in our bilateral connection agreement with the National Energy System Operator (formerly National Grid ESO). Of course, given the CMU is an interconnector there are a variety of sites which are owned/managed by Eleclink and relate to the CMU, as additional information we have provided details of those sites below. Description of CMU Components:
Viking Link is a HVDC interconnector between GB and Danish transmission systems. 
Viking Link involved the construction of two converter stations, sited in GB and Denmark. At the converter stations, alternating current electricity from the sending end is converted to direct current electricity and transmitted through the cables. The direct current electricity is converted into alternating current at the receiving end, before it is transmitted to consumers via the onshore electricity networks in GB and Denmark.
In GB, the grid connection point for Viking Link is at Bicker Fen substation. The converter station at North Ing Drove is 2km from the substation which is connected via AC underground cables. From the converter station, the British onshore section covers 68km of HVDC underground cable to the landfall point of Boygrift which marks the beginning of the offshore route. The marine section of the link has a total of 621km from Boygrift to the Danish landing point of Blaabjerg through British, Dutch, German and Danish waters. From the Danish landfall point in Blaabjerg the Danish onshore section of Viking Link covers 76km of HVDC underground cable to the converter station which is adjacent to the Revsing substation.
Location and Post Code: Viking Link Ltd, Bicker Fen Converter Station, Northorpe Road, Donington SPALDING PE11 4XY
